In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of genomic resources and tools to facilitate future studies of cotton.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cotton genome is highly dynamic, with frequent gene conversion events between the A and D subgenomes, as well as frequent deletions and duplications within both subgenomes, and that the cotton polyploid genome has undergone extensive reorganization since its origin.
the A1, A2 and D5 genomes are highly conserved in terms of their gene content and gene order.
the G. hirsutum genome is an amalgamation of the G. arboreum and G. raimondii genomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genome sequence of cotton is not yet fully resolved.
the A1, A2, and D5 genome sequences are now available for use in cotton breeding and genetic research.
this is a very nice study of the G. hirsutum genome and its diploid ancestors, and it will be very useful in future studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
whole-genome sequencing of multiple accessions from each diploid species provides a robust reference genome for the A and D genomes of the polyploid species, Gossypium.
the genome of the allopolyploids is not a simple mosaic of the two diploid genomes.
the G. raimondii reference genome is a good reference sequence to map reads for other diploid species, but it is not a good reference sequence for polyploid species.
